Work in C:\Users\edmem\kodely-prod (Next.js 16 + Prisma, an AI website builder called Kodely).

BUILD: click-to-edit on the preview canvas. The board card calls it "the difference between a toy and a tool for non-devs", and it is the highest-value unbuilt item in Builder/Editor UX.

## What it is
Click an element in the live preview, and either edit it directly (text) or tell the AI about *that specific element* ("make this bigger", "change this photo") without describing where it is in words. Today every change costs a full generation and the user has to say "the heading in the second section" and hope.

## The architecture, and the hard part
Read these before designing anything:
- `app/projects/[id]/PreviewFrame.tsx` and `Editor.tsx` — the preview is an `<iframe>` pointed at `/api/preview/[id]/...`.
- `app/api/preview/[id]/[[...path]]/route.ts` — **the iframe is sandboxed `allow-scripts allow-forms` WITHOUT `allow-same-origin`.** That is deliberate and correct (the security audit specifically praised it). It means the parent page **cannot reach into the iframe's DOM**. `contentDocument` is null. Any design that assumes DOM access from the parent is dead on arrival — check this yourself before building.
- The CSP served with the preview is `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; ... connect-src 'none'; form-action 'self'; base-uri 'none'`. Note `connect-src 'none'`.
- `lib/build-site.ts` — the preview serves COMPILED Vite output, not source. So an element in the DOM has no direct line back to the JSX that produced it.

So the two real questions are: **how does the parent learn what was clicked**, and **how does a clicked DOM node map back to source you can edit**. `postMessage` works across an opaque origin — verify what the sandbox actually permits rather than assuming. Injecting a small script into the served preview HTML is possible (`'unsafe-inline'` is already allowed) but the injection point is in a route file outside your scope; if that is what you need, say so precisely.

**Do not fake it.** If a full round trip is not achievable within scope, build the part that is and report exactly what is missing. A selection UI that cannot actually target an element is worse than nothing.

## Prefer the honest subset
A realistic first version: click selects an element, the parent shows what was selected (tag, text snippet, position), and the prompt box is pre-filled with a precise reference so the model can find it — turning "make the heading bigger" into something unambiguous. Direct text editing without a generation is a bonus, not the requirement.

## Scope — YOU MAY ONLY CREATE/EDIT FILES UNDER `app/projects/[id]/`
Everything else is off limits. READ anything.

## Do not regress
`Editor.tsx` carries: live progress narration, the building overlay, thumbs-up/down, zip download, Enhance/Revert, low-credit warning, Stop/cancel, device-frame preview, a Cmd/Ctrl-K command palette, connection-loss recovery, a cost estimate, and an SEO panel. **All of it must keep working.** Read the file fully first.

Traps already hit in this exact file — do not repeat them:
- Two `aria-live` regions holding the same string made screen readers announce every progress line twice.
- The command palette went keyboard-dead when focus was outside the dialog; it needs the window-level Escape net that is there now.
- Copy must not claim behaviour that isn't real.

## Constraints
- **Do not weaken the iframe sandbox.** Adding `allow-same-origin` would let generated customer code reach the parent origin. That is a security regression and is not an acceptable shortcut — the audit calls the current setting out as easy to get wrong and done right.
- Preserve the accessibility bar: `focus-visible:` states, real labels, `aria-*` on stateful controls, no keyboard traps. Selection must be operable by keyboard, not mouse-only.
- **No new white text on the brand gradient** (fails contrast — known accepted issue). Match the existing idiom.
- Known pre-existing issue: the sidebar is `w-96` so there is horizontal overflow at 380px. Do not worsen it; do not attempt the responsive rework.
- No new npm dependencies. Do NOT run `npm run build`, `git commit`, `git push`, or `deploy.sh`.
- **HARD GATE: `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint app lib components` must BOTH be clean — currently ZERO errors and ZERO warnings.**
- A dev server may be on :3003. The Browser pane may not composite frames, so verify DOM and computed styles programmatically rather than by screenshot.

## Report back
What you verified about the sandbox (specifically: what the parent can and cannot do to that iframe), the mechanism you chose, exactly what works end to end versus what is stubbed, anything you need outside your scope, and confirmation the existing editor features still work.

content.text:
Done. Cleaned up all harness processes and temp data; no stray files in the repo.

## What I verified about the sandbox (measured, not assumed)

I could not use the Browser pane — it silently refuses to load any iframe carrying a `sandbox` attribute without `allow-same-origin`, so nothing renders there. I instead drove real headless Chrome (CDP over Node's built-in WebSocket) against servers reproducing the preview's exact sandbox + CSP.

**Parent → iframe:** `contentDocument` is `null`; `contentWindow.location` and `.document` both throw `SecurityError`. `contentWindow.postMessage(msg, "*")` **does** get through. Targeting an exact origin is silently dropped; `targetOrigin: "null"` throws `SyntaxError`. So `"*"` is mandatory.

**Iframe → parent:** works. `event.origin` arrives as the literal string `"null"` — worthless for auth. `event.source === iframe.contentWindow` is the only real check, and even that only proves *the frame* sent it, not *our agent*.

**Three findings that changed the design:**
1. Built `index.html` references `/assets/index-*.js` absolutely. `GET /assets/…` on the app origin is a **404** (published sites work only because `proxy.ts` rewrites the sites domain; there is no equivalent for the editor).
2. **Every subresource request from inside the opaque-origin frame is `sec-fetch-site: cross-site` and carries no cookie.** A cookie-authenticated `/api/preview/[id]/assets/…` therefore 401s. There is no header-only fix.
3. Vite emits `<script type="module" crossorigin>`; module scripts are always CORS-mode, so they additionally need `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`. Stripping `crossorigin` does not help (verified).

**Any one of those makes the preview blank. The in-editor preview has never rendered anything** — no CSS, no JS, just `<div id="root">`. That is a pre-existing bug, not something I introduced.

## Mechanism

The parent (where cookies work) fetches `index.html` + assets, **inlines** them into one self-contained document, injects the selection agent, and hands it to the iframe via `srcdoc`. Zero subresources means zero cross-site requests. The `sandbox` attribute is **byte-identical** — still `allow-scripts allow-forms`, still opaque origin, `contentDocument` still `null` (re-checked on the live frame at the end of the run). No out-of-scope file was needed.

Because a `srcdoc` document has no response headers, the policy travels in-band as `<meta http-equiv>`, first child of `<head>`. It is **stricter** than the header it replaces (`default-src 'none'`, everything inlined). Verified: an external `<script src>` is blocked and never requested, and `fetch()` rejects.

## What works end to end

Against a real generated site (Copperleaf Tea Room, real 204KB bundle), with a real CDP mouse click:

```
Change the <h1> element reading "A quiet room, a warm pot, and time to slow down."
in section 2 of 5 ("A quiet room, a warm pot, and time to slow down."),
at section#top > div > div:nth-of-type(1) > h1:
```

Click-select, hover outline, in-frame arrow keys (parent/child/sibling), Escape to exit, parent-driven move buttons, clear, and the prompt pre-fill all verified working. **The preview now actually renders** as a side effect.

Two defects the E2E run caught and I fixed: in-frame keys never reached the agent (the pick cancels the click, so focus never entered — added an agent-owned focus sink, no `tabindex` on generated elements); and containers reported run-together `textContent` ("Since 2014A quiet room") as if it were their own text — now own-text vs. subtree is distinguished, and the reference says *"a container whose contents begin…"* rather than *"reading"*, using source-faithful casing so the string is greppable.

**Not built:** direct text editing without a generation. Editing text means editing JSX and rebuilding — a server round trip with no endpoint in scope. Every change still goes through a normal build, and the UI copy says exactly that.

## Files

New: `app/projects/[id]/preview-agent.ts`, `app/projects/[id]/SelectionPanel.tsx`. Modified: `PreviewFrame.tsx`, `Editor.tsx`, `page.tsx`.

## Judgment call for review

Feeding the iframe `srcdoc` instead of `src` is a real change to how the preview is served, made entirely inside my scope. It is what makes the feature possible *and* fixes the blank preview. Trade-off: the preview document can no longer load any external resource at all — previously it couldn't either, so nothing regresses, but a future generated site wanting a non-`data:` image would need `img-src` widened.

Also worth flagging: generated content can forge a `selected` message. Bounded by `normalizeSelection` (validates and clamps every field), text-only rendering, and never auto-submitting — worst case is editable text appearing in the prompt box.

## Coordinator's two additions

Both done. `BrandKitPanel` mounted as a fifth "Brand" view with `onSaved={refreshFiles}`. Submissions link added next to Publish **with** a live unread count — `page.tsx` is inside my scope, so I added a `db.formSubmission.count` using the same `readAt: null, spam: false` filter the submissions page uses, no fragile plumbing. Both also added to the command palette so it doesn't go stale.

## Regression check

Read `Editor.tsx` in full first. Untouched and intact: progress narration, building overlay, thumbs-up/down, zip download, Enhance/Revert, low-credit warning, Stop/cancel, device-frame preview, ⌘K palette (window-level Escape net preserved), connection-loss recovery, cost estimate, SEO panel. Still exactly one `aria-live` for progress — the selection summary's region is separate and cannot be active simultaneously (the overlay covers the preview during builds). No new white-on-gradient text; `focus-visible:` rings on every new control; selection is fully keyboard-operable from the editor's own tab order, not just inside the frame.

**Gates:** `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npx eslint app lib components` **0 errors 0 warnings**, tests **209/209 pass**. Both `/projects/[id]` and `/projects/[id]/submissions` compile and 307 to login on the dev server.

## Recommended follow-up (outside my scope)

`app/api/preview/[id]/[[...path]]/route.ts` carries a comment claiming `form-action 'self'` is effectively `'none'` because `'self'` matches nothing in an opaque origin. I measured the opposite: `'self'` resolves to the serving origin and the policy works as written. Worth correcting so nobody relies on the wrong model.
